candidate.title: ClickSeq
candidate.scope: The ClickSeq row of the supplied Illumina poster crop, from RNA through the PCR-amplified cDNA library, interpreted at schematic scope using the original Routh et al. ClickSeq paper (PMID 26116762). The visible labels are ClickSeq; RNA; Add semi-random primers and AzNTPs - dNTP mixture; Purify single-stranded cDNA; Click-ligate alkyne-modified adaptor; PCR amplify; and cDNA library. The left description identifies stochastically terminated 3′-azido-blocked cDNA. Five rightward arrows connect one serial route. Repeated RNA/cDNA glyphs illustrate a population and variable fragment lengths within that route; no labeled alternative, split or pooling junction is drawn. CaptureSeq, RASL-seq and the partial 3Seq/3-Seq/3′-end-seq row are neighboring poster entries, not ClickSeq alternatives. The partly clipped chemical cartoons at the far right do not supply an additional workflow. The checked collection page is explicitly headed ClickSeq and reproduces these stages; its associated-kit listings and the paper’s validation experiments do not expand the workflow targets. Sequencing and analysis are readout context, not additional depicted operations.

states.label: PCR-amplified cDNA library
features: Paired DNA strands with adaptor-colored segments are the final product depicted.
RNA sequence information is carried by the amplified cDNA inserts, sampled from internal RNA positions by priming and stochastic termination.
Fragment boundaries arise during cDNA synthesis; they do not by themselves identify native RNA ends.
The primary paper used these libraries for Illumina sequencing of viral RNA and host mRNA.

operations.label: Add semi-random primers and AzNTPs - dNTP mixture
operations.description: Use RNA as template to synthesize adaptor-bearing cDNA from semi-random priming sites. Incorporation of an AzNTP stops extension and leaves a 3′-azido-blocked cDNA fragment. This composite schematic block includes the reverse transcription clarified by the paper, rather than merely mixing reagents.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription with dNTPs and chain-terminating 3′-azido-2′,3′-dideoxynucleotides; RNA is copied rather than fragmented to create the cDNA population.
operations.information_effect: The cDNA sequence records a segment of its RNA template and acquires a primer-derived Illumina adaptor region. Stochastic termination generates distributed cDNA endpoints without physical fragmentation of the source RNA.

operations.label: Purify single-stranded cDNA
operations.description: Recover the single-stranded, 3′-azido-blocked cDNA population from the reverse-transcription reaction. The diagram omits the RNA template from the recovered material; the paper specifies removal of unincorporated AzNTPs.
operations.mechanism: Purification of the cDNA reaction product, retaining the reactive azido termini; the schematic does not specify a separate RNA-removal chemistry.
operations.information_effect: Carries the RNA-derived cDNA inserts and primer-derived adaptor region forward in a purified single-stranded material.

operations.label: Click-ligate alkyne-modified adaptor
operations.description: Covalently attach the alkyne-modified adaptor to each captured 3′-azido cDNA end, creating single-stranded DNA flanked by both adaptor regions.
operations.mechanism: Copper(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition between the cDNA 3′-azido group and adaptor 5′-hexynyl group creates a triazole linkage. Copper-associated catalysts are reaction components, not transferred library molecules.
operations.information_effect: Supplies the second adaptor interface to the RNA-derived insert. The complementary reactive end groups favor cDNA-to-adaptor joining rather than cDNA-to-cDNA joining; this does not establish complete capture or eliminate every source of chimera.

evidence.locator: b00019, library capture limitation
evidence.quote: While approximately 10 % of the 3’-azido-blocked cDNA fragments in Figure 2B could be ligated to an alkyne-modified oligo, the conversion of this triazole-linked ssDNA into a double stranded DNA via the read-through of the triazole-linkage seems to be far less efficient.

operations.label: PCR amplify
operations.description: Amplify the adaptor-flanked, click-ligated ssDNA to produce the depicted double-stranded cDNA library. Initial copying must traverse the triazole junction to recover an amplifiable insert.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper demonstrates polymerase read-through of the unnatural triazole linkage and subsequent PCR with adaptor-directed primers. The demonstrated compatibility is inefficient and does not establish compatibility with every polymerase.
operations.information_effect: The sequencing carrier is amplified DNA representing sampled RNA segments. Sequence reads can identify RNA-derived sequence and supported sequence junctions; the schematic does not measure intact RNA molecules directly. Inefficient click capture and especially triazole read-through limit recovery, so the output is not evidence that every starting RNA molecule is represented.

Full-text b00005-b00007 and Figure 1C describe semi-random reverse transcription, azido termination, purification, alkyne-adaptor click-ligation and PCR, supporting all four local operations. Template-specific chemistry demonstrations and comparator library preparations in the paper are not alternative target workflows in this schematic.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the complete scoped architecture, including all eight materials, four operations and eleven routes. The two template/cDNA glyphs illustrate a population within one workflow; there are no labeled separate fractions, split, pooling junction, attachment or compartment transitions. Each operation agrees with its outgoing state and receiving interface. The final arrow identifies the PCR library without another transformation. Scope, carrier identity, reactive-end changes, limitations and both paper assessments are supported. The candidate distinguishes the poster’s click-stage reactant symbols from the paper-established covalent product; no consequential correction or blocking unknown remains.
